_note: Exercises for the live lessons, keyed by module number. When the teacher adds a lesson for a module, the site copies these items into it. A null 'correct' marks a question with no right answer. The teacher can add more items during a lesson.

1.label: Warm-up quiz
1.question: Which way of producing code have you used most so far?
options: Asking a chat assistant for snippets.
Directing an agent that edits the project.

1.label: After block 1
1.question: How does this course treat agentic software engineering?
options: As a discipline with durable principles, a method that can be learned, and characteristic faults.
As a set of tools that write code faster than a person can.
As a way to replace programmers with agents.
As a style of writing prompts.

1.label: After block 2
1.question: What does the long line of handovers describe?
options: How programming moved from hand-written code to directing an agent.
How code passes from developers to testers.
How a team divides a project into tasks.

1.label: After block 3
1.question: What rhythm does the course set for every piece of work?
options: Equip the agent, then verify its work.
Write the code, then ask the agent to explain it.
Plan for a week, then build for a week.
Let the agent work, and review only if the tests fail.

1.label: After block 4
1.question: Which tension does this course set out to answer?
options: The speed of production has outrun our ability to trust the result.
Models are still too expensive for everyday coding.
Most developers refuse to hand work to an agent.
Agents cannot yet write code that compiles.

9.label: Warm-up quiz
9.question: In module 8, who supplies the why of an interface specification?

9.label: After block 1
9.question: What does the course call cognified software?
options: Software with a model reasoning inside it.
Software that learns from its users' clicks.

9.label: After block 2
9.question: What does module 9 ask you to make visible for every model call?
options: The source code of the model.
The name of the person who wrote the prompt.
The number of agents in the session.

9.label: After block 3
9.question: Why does a product that calls a model need a ceiling?
options: To stop a runaway process before it spends too much money and time.
To keep the model's answers short.
To meet a legal limit on model use.
To make the agent work faster.

9.label: After block 4
9.question: What groundwork does module 9 lay for the rest of the course?
options: The economic groundwork for building anything that calls a model.
The security model of the running project.
The design of the user interface.
